text:
alex: Heads-up — canary showing a regression after last night's merge (PR #4123). Short-seq workload p95 decode is up ~35% vs baseline. Putting the canary on hold.
deploy-bot: Canary autoscaler detected p95 spike for service=runtime-prod, holding rollout and notifying #eng-runtime.
sarah: Quick findings: KV cache hit-rate dropped noticeably on the failing canary nodes. Eviction storms and increased small-batch churn. Logs show a lot more prefix cache misses around the same time as the merge.
maya: Starting a local bisect now. Command: `git bisect start --term-old=good --term-new=bad 9f4c2f..HEAD` — initial suspect is the fused-op selection change that landed in 9f4c2f.
perf-bot: CI perf job runtime-ci/perf FAILED on commit 9f4c2f: decode p95 +28% (short-seq test). See: https://ci.internal/reports/9f4c2f
alex: Perf snapshot (canary node):
```
before: p95=42ms p50=12ms kv_hit=0.89
after:  p95=57ms p50=13ms kv_hit=0.64
hotspots: attention_kernel_choose + memcpy_async + batcher::assemble
```
ryan: If bisect points at 9f4c2f I'll open an emergency revert. Also: we may be choosing the fused attention kernel for sequences <=64 due to the new selector heuristic. That would explain the memcpy/misaligned work.
maya: Bisect progress: narrowed to 9f4c2f -> 3a7d1e. Repro locally with the short-seq harness (`make perf-harness && ./harness --seq-max=48 --warm=1000`). 9f4c2f introduces `batcher::prefer_fused_for_latency` toggle and a tweak to prefetch thresholds.
sarah: I dumped KV eviction traces: batcher is prefetching more KV pages, causing front-loaded memory pressure and earlier evictions. Hit-rate drop matches timeframe of the fused selector change. Prefetch seems to be triggered by a new heuristic that treats small batches as long sequences.
alex: pprof flame (top lines):
```
30.2% attention_kernel_choose()
18.7% memcpy_async
12.4% batcher::assemble_batches
6.9% kv_cache::evict_if_needed
```
ryan: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) flip the default of `prefer_fused_for_latency` -> false; 2) add a guard in kernel selector: if seq_len <= 64 prefer small-kernel; 3) patch prefetch threshold to the prior value. Which do we want for the emergency revert?
maya: I'll prepare a targeted revert PR that only removes the fused selector change and restores the previous prefetch threshold. Add tests for seq-length routing. Pushing branch `hotfix/revert-fused-selector` now.
perf-bot: Perf CI rerun queued for `hotfix/revert-fused-selector`. Will post results when done.
deploy-bot: Canary hold remains active. Manual resume disabled until patch merges + perf green.
sarah: One more datapoint: sample traces show attention_fused_v2 kernel increases device-to-host memcpy calls (small batches cause many tiny launches). That accounts for the memcpy hotspot.
alex: Plan: maya opens PR (WIP), ryan prepares emergency revert if PR not ready in 45m. After merge we run the short-seq perf harness + canary smoke. I'll file rollout-blocker with logs & perf diffs.
maya: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4123-revert-fused-selector (WIP). Added unit test for seq routing and a regression test for kv hit-rate on the harness.
ryan: I'll stand by to cut the revert if CI still shows regressions. Also adding a safety flag to disable aggressive prefetch in runtime config.
alex: Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick triage. Please post perf CI link here when available. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: Rerun complete: `hotfix/revert-fused-selector` -> perf delta p95 = +2% (within noise). Job: https://ci.internal/reports/hotfix-4123
maya: Merged revert and added tests. Monitoring canary after resume.
deploy-bot: Canary resumed by automation after manual approval. Observability hooks enabled.
sarah: Early canary metrics look back to baseline: kv_hit ~0.88, p95 ~44ms.
alex: Closing rollout blocker once we see stable p95 for 30m. Great work — quick bisect + revert saved us from a longer outage.
